plans.title: Fix alembic migration TypeError: Union descriptor __getitem__ (Python 3.14 + SQLAlchemy 2.0.36)
plans.purpose: Fix alembic upgrade head TypeError caused by PEP 604 union syntax (str | None) in SQLAlchemy models incompatible with Python 3.14 runtime.
learnings: When SQLAlchemy declarative models raise TypeError: descriptor '__getitem__' requires a 'typing.Union' object but received a 'tuple' on Python 3.14, the fix is NOT rewriting `X | None` to `Optional[X]` (both trigger the same code path) — it's upgrading the sqlalchemy pin. SQLAlchemy 2.0.36 predates Python 3.14 support; support began at 2.0.41 with further annotation fixes through later 2.0.x patches. Always check runtime Python version against library's supported-version history first for this class of typing/annotation errors.

plans.scope_in: Pin bcrypt to a passlib-1.7.4-compatible version in backend/requirements.txt; user reinstalls and retests registration.
plans.scope_out: Not upgrading passlib itself or switching hashing libraries; not touching frontend register() error-handling logic (correct as-is once backend returns valid JSON).
plans.why: app/core/security.py uses passlib.context.CryptContext(schemes=[\"bcrypt\"]) to hash passwords. passlib 1.7.4 (pinned, released 2020) probes bcrypt.__about__.__version__ to identify the backend version; this attribute was removed starting bcrypt 4.1. Since requirements.txt pins passlib[bcrypt]==1.7.4 without pinning bcrypt itself, pip resolved bcrypt to the latest 5.0.0, which lacks __about__, causing an AttributeError inside hash_password() during POST /auth/register. FastAPI's default 500 handling under the dev server does not always guarantee a JSON body in this crash path, so the frontend's requests.Response.json() call fails with JSONDecodeError when trying to parse the non-JSON error body.

plans.title: Fix DataError: invalid input value for enum userrole "RESEARCHER" on registration
plans.purpose: Fix psycopg.errors.InvalidTextRepresentation surfacing as sqlalchemy.exc.DataError during POST /auth/register, caused by SQLAlchemy sending the Python enum member NAME instead of its lowercase VALUE to the native Postgres enum column.

steps.content: Add values_callable to the SQLAlchemy Enum(UserRole) column in app/models/user.py so it persists enum .value (lowercase) instead of .name (uppercase), matching the Postgres native enum labels.
steps.implementation_outline: Change `Enum(UserRole)` to `Enum(UserRole, values_callable=lambda enum_cls: [member.value for member in enum_cls])` on the `role` column in app/models/user.py, so SQLAlchemy sends the enum's lowercase .value (matching Postgres labels: researcher, institution_admin, reviewer, system_admin) instead of the uppercase .name.

plans.scope_in: Fix app/models/user.py's role column definition to persist enum VALUES (lowercase) instead of NAMES, matching the existing Postgres enum labels. No new migration needed since Postgres enum labels are already correct.
plans.scope_out: Not touching the migration file (Postgres enum labels already match the model's intended values); not touching frontend register() error handling.
plans.why: app/models/user.py defines `class UserRole(str, enum.Enum): RESEARCHER = "researcher", ...` and the column as `Enum(UserRole)`. SQLAlchemy's Enum type, by default, persists the Python enum member's NAME (e.g. "RESEARCHER") to native DB enum columns, not its .value. But the Postgres enum type `userrole` (created in alembic/versions/0001_initial.py) only has the lowercase labels: researcher, institution_admin, reviewer, system_admin. So inserting a new user fails with InvalidTextRepresentation because "RESEARCHER" (uppercase) is not a valid label for that Postgres enum type.

plans.title: Validate institution_id in /researchers/me to avoid raw 500 on bad foreign key
plans.purpose: Prevent unhandled IntegrityError (ForeignKeyViolation) crashes on POST/PUT /researchers/me when institution_id doesn't exist in the institutions table, by validating it upfront and returning a clean 400.

steps.content: Add an Institution existence check in researchers.py: query Institution by payload.institution_id before create/update; raise HTTPException(400, 'Institution not found') if it doesn't exist and institution_id is not None.
steps.implementation_outline: Added a `_validate_institution_id(db, institution_id)` helper in researchers.py that queries the Institution table by id and raises HTTPException(400, f"Institution {institution_id} not found") if the id is not None and no matching row exists. Called this helper before db.commit() in both create_my_profile (POST /me) and update_my_profile (PUT /me), ahead of the ORM mutation, so the FK check happens as a clean validation step instead of failing mid-transaction at commit time.
steps.verification: Code review of researchers.py -> confirmed _validate_institution_id(db, payload.institution_id) is called before db.commit() in both POST /me and PUT /me handlers, returning HTTPException 400 'Institution {id} not found' when the institution_id doesn't exist, and skipping the check entirely (no-op) when institution_id is None -> PASS. Must-fail check: removing the call would let a bad institution_id reach db.commit() and surface as an unhandled IntegrityError/500 again, which is exactly the bug this step fixes.
steps.outcome: Verified by reading the current contents of backend/app/api/routes/researchers.py: the _validate_institution_id helper already exists and is already invoked in both create_my_profile and update_my_profile prior to db.commit(). No code change was needed this pass — the fix was already present in the working tree.
